title: Offset+
tagline: Offset surfaces, or curves, toward the side a reference is on -- surfaces of opposite orientation all move the same way, and curves offset in the frame you choose.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: The built-in offset surface goes along the normal, and the built-in offset curve works in a sketch plane with a flip. Offset+ offsets each surface body toward the reference's side of it, and offsets 3D curves in a transport, surface-normal or plane frame -- toward the reference too.
useWhen: Surfaces from different sources face different ways
A 3D edge chain needs a constant offset (along a surface, lifted off it, or in plan)
Corners of the chain must be rounded or trimmed cleanly
slides.caption: Offset+ open on the ski topsheet: offset 2 mm toward the plane 'Below ski'.

slides.title: Why a reference instead of a flip

points.head: A flip is about a normal
points.body: 'Front', 'opposite direction', 'Thickness 1' all mean: relative to the normal -- and normals change freely upstream.

points.head: A reference is about the model
points.body: Pick geometry on the side you mean. The choice survives any change of orientation.

points.head: Drop-in
points.body: With no reference, the feature behaves exactly like the built-in.

points.head: Transport frame
points.body: The direction is carried along the chain without twisting -- a helix offset 'toward the axis' stays inside (test C7).

points.head: Surface normal / plane
points.body: Off a surface, along it, or in the plane perpendicular to a direction (plan view).

points.head: Corners
points.body: A gap on the outside gets an arc (radius = the distance); an overlap on the inside is trimmed to the crossing (test C8).

slides.title: The dialog: surfaces
params: SURFACE: offset surface bodies. CURVE: offset edges or wires (next slides).
Each body is offset toward the reference's side of THAT body.
Geometry on the side to offset toward. Empty = the arrow alone (a plain flip).
The arrow. On: toward the reference. Off: away from it.
Print details: which way each body or chain went, corners and fits.

slides.title: The dialog: curves, plane frame
params: Connected edges form one chain; each chain becomes one wire.
Plane frame: the offset lies in planes perpendicular to this. Empty = world Z (a plan-view offset).
Here the Front plane: every chain moves toward it.
Samples per edge (24), Max station spacing (5 mm), Fit tolerance (0.001 mm).

slides.title: The dialog: curves, surface-normal frame
params: Surface normal: the direction comes from a surface at each point.
The surface whose normals define the offset (its orientation does not matter: normals are kept continuous).
Along surface normal: lift the curve off the surface. Along surface: stay in it, perpendicular to the curve.
slides.note: On the topsheet edge chain all three frames land at y 70 (5 mm in): the topsheet is flat across its width there. They differ on twisted chains and curved surfaces (tests C5-C7).

slides.title: Example: surface offset
slides.head: Topsheet offset 2 mm toward 'Below ski' (topsheet_surf studio)
slides.body: The topsheet faces down, into the ski. Offset+ reads which side of the topsheet 'Below ski' is on and offsets that way -- if the topsheet's normal flipped upstream, the offset would still go down. The offset surface keeps the topsheet's orientation (still facing down).

keys: Curves: the ends of each wire (start = the end at the source's start).
Curves: the edge at each end.
Curves: the arcs that round the outside corners.
Surfaces: the open boundary edges of the offset surfaces.
messages: The corner counts are reported here only (not published).
N corner(s) could not be closed ... The wire has a gap at each.
A corner sharper than the offset allows, or skew 3D pieces. Reduce the distance or split the chain there.
The side reference is not to either side of chain k in this frame
The reference lies along the curve or on the surface. Move it off to one side.
The curve runs along the plane / surface normal
No offset direction exists there in that frame.

items.head: Use a local reference
items.body: A mate connector or vertex near the geometry, on the side meant.

items.head: Transport for 3D chains
items.body: It never flips at an inflection and never twists, so the offset stays on the side it started.

items.head: Outputs keep their input's orientation
items.body: The reference picks the side, not the normal. Built-ins downstream that follow the normal (Thicken, Offset surface, Move face) need Orient to reference first -- or use the reference-side feature instead.

items.head: Sharp corners and large distances
items.body: Where the offsets neither separate nor cross cleanly the corner is left open, with a warning.
